subject: Windvale Language 1.0 compiler and Slice 8 paired-host qualification
claim: Source commit 47dd3d69fef8a0ac5b894885b0a1917e21033622 passed the complete selected qualification workflow. Each of the Windows and Debian hosts passed 126 native owners and 5,981 cases across four independent shards; the exact compiler reconstructed deterministically on both hosts; the declared native WebAssembly subset passed on both hosts; and the final aggregate gate accepted every required job. The qualified cases include the real Linux system-profile Foreign record consumer, the Windows and Linux native ABI paths, all 57 database-storage cases per host, the repaired Linux segmented-cache process race, and the repaired Windows file-read cleanup boundary.

runs.target: Complete selected Windows and Linux qualification and aggregate verification gate

limitations: This qualifies the frozen Language 1.0 compiler scope and bounded Slice 8 contracts at the named source commit. It does not qualify unfinished Libraries 1.0 profiles, WVDB 1.0, integrated services, Windvale OS, installers, or a v1.0.0 release.
The WebAssembly jobs qualify their explicitly declared subset; they do not imply that every native x64 system-profile or Foreign operation is portable to WebAssembly.

The real Foreign record consumer is Linux system-profile source. Windows validates and cross-compiles that exact source path while Linux performs its native SysV execution; separate Windows-native Foreign ABI cases qualify the Windows path.

The qualification establishes correctness at this source identity, not acceptable development feedback latency. In particular, database-storage passed all 57 cases on both hosts but remains a named verification-performance improvement.
This evidence was produced and reviewed within the project and has not received external audit or certification.
